text: The passage repays attention to what it withholds. Sarah has no place in Genesis 22; in the very next verse the book records her death. The scene therefore intimates, though it never declares, that something in the household has not survived the mountain. Abraham comes back to the servants, and Isaac is not named with him. At the very point at which a poorer tale would have detained us, the narration passes on; its silence belongs to the account of Abraham and Isaac.
